text: right. effectively the entire thing needs to behave like you treat dirty rectangles
resolution: Implemented live dirty-rectangle erase so a moved/deleted baked piece's old geometry clears WITHOUT a rebake (the cleanup-speed complaint). The editor pushes the dirty piece's old-footprint AABB; the loader erases the baked geometry inside it: batched box/wall/floor/ramp instance rows collapse (scale->0) and re-upload IN PLACE via a new scene-node version (covers both the monolithic and streaming/per-chunk paths; flora skipped), and baked mesh-prop ('pepes') node ranges hide by position (the MOVE twin of the req_1845 coincident re-skin hide). One rect mechanism, both geometry classes — answering 'why aren't building pieces referenced like props': they ARE instances, just batched for draw-call scale, so they needed a position handle not a different encoding. The live overlay draws the new position; the settle bake still trails behind for /compiled colliders but no longer gates the visual. Erases dedup by signature (a plain placement never re-stages the static world) and clear+re-baseline on reload. Framework: scene3d_instance_version + in-place static re-upload (framework/gpu/3d.zig); new __compiled_world_set_dirty_erase door. Verified: ReleaseFast compiles and the streaming render proof stays GREEN; live move/delete is the user's by-feel check after a dev-host restart (Zig changed).
